title: Taiwan Dollar Poised for Rally Despite AI Sector Selloff
summary: Taiwan's currency faces AI-driven selloffs, but analysts forecast 3% rally to year-end on record trade surplus and semiconductor strength. Economic resilience
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Taiwan dollar weakened to April 2025 lows amid record foreign equity outflows driven by AI valuation concerns and semiconductor sector uncertainty.
- Analysts forecast 3% currency appreciation to 31.50-31.60 per USD by year-end 2026, supported by record $70 billion trade surplus and 10% GDP growth.
- Central bank expected to maintain 31.5-32.5 trading range while underlying AI chip export demand and current account strength support medium-term recovery.


Taiwan's currency is weathering intense pressure from global AI sector volatility, but major financial institutions are projecting a sharp rebound into year-end 2026. Despite recent weakness that pushed the Taiwan dollar to its lowest level since April 2025, analysts at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. and ING Bank forecast appreciation of approximately 3% from current levels, targeting 31.50 to 31.60 per US dollar by December.


The disconnect between short-term currency weakness and medium-term bullish forecasts reflects Taiwan's underlying economic fundamentals, which remain exceptionally strong even as global investors retreat from AI-related equities. The island's current account surplus reached a record high near $70 billion in late 2025, driven by unprecedented demand for advanced semiconductors, and officials have raised the full-year economic growth forecast above 10%, marking Taiwan's first double-digit expansion since 2010.


## Record Foreign Outflows Drive Currency Weakness


Foreign investors sold NT$302.6 billion ($9.3 billion) of Taiwan equities on Thursday, the largest daily outflow on record, according to market data. The selling pressure came as global markets grappled with concerns over lofty AI stock valuations and the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Officially released on October 18, 2026, the latest currency data showed the Taiwan dollar testing its year-to-date low around 32.50 per US dollar.


Lin Li, head of global markets research for Asia at MUFG Bank, noted the conflicting forces at play. "Record trade surpluses and AI-related exports continue to generate underlying Taiwan dollar support," Li said. "But foreign portfolio outflows, outward investment and the large US dollar-Taiwan dollar yield differential is creating offsetting US dollar demand at the moment." Li projects the currency will appreciate to 31.8 per greenback by year-end before strengthening further to 30.9 by June 2027.


## Central Bank Intervention Expectations


Market participants are closely watching the Central Bank of the Republic of China (CBC) for signs of intervention to stabilize the currency. While analysts do not view the 32.50 level as a rigid defense line, most agree the monetary authority has been comfortable maintaining a 31.5 to 32.5 trading range throughout 2026.


"The CBC will attempt to keep the Taiwan dollar relatively rangebound," said Lynn Song, chief economist for Greater China at ING Bank. "I don't think it is a firm line in the sand to defend, but it does seem that 31.5-32.5 range has been comfortable for them so far this year." Jiuk Choi, Asia Pacific macro strategist at State Street Bank & Trust, added that policymakers are more likely to focus on reducing volatility rather than defending specific levels.


## Semiconductor Earnings as Key Catalyst


Currency traders are closely monitoring earnings reports from major semiconductor manufacturers as the next critical catalyst for cross-border flows. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. delivered a better-than-expected revenue outlook on Thursday, though the positive news failed to fully calm broader market anxieties over AI capital expenditure sustainability and Chinese competition in advanced chip manufacturing.


"Upcoming global tech earnings could increase Taiwan dollar volatility, particularly given the market's heightened sensitivity to AI-related capex, profitability, and Chinese competition," Choi noted. Despite near-term headwinds, he forecasts a recovery to 31.80 per US dollar by December 2026.


## Structural Factors Supporting Currency Strength


Beyond cyclical market sentiment, several structural factors favor Taiwan dollar appreciation over the medium term:


- Taiwan's current account surplus remains robust despite recent narrowing from record highs
- AI-driven semiconductor demand continues to support export revenues
- The island's technology sector maintains a dominant position in advanced chip manufacturing
- Taiwan's currency exhibits among the lowest volatility rates in emerging markets


Elevated crude oil prices and a hawkish Federal Reserve pose near-term challenges. US 10-year Treasury yields currently sit roughly 300 basis points above similar-tenor Taiwanese sovereign bonds, creating yield differentials that support dollar strength. However, Trang Le, foreign exchange and rates specialist at LGT Private Banking, argues these headwinds are temporary. "Strong export momentum, robust external balances and the AI-driven semiconductor cycle leave the medium-term bias tilted toward Taiwan dollar appreciation," Le said.


## What This Means


The Taiwan dollar's current weakness represents a short-term dislocation driven by global risk sentiment rather than deteriorating fundamentals. With the island's economy on track for double-digit growth and semiconductor exports remaining resilient, analysts view recent currency levels as attractive entry points for positioning ahead of an expected year-end rally. Market participants should expect continued volatility around major tech earnings releases, but the underlying trajectory favors appreciation as AI infrastructure buildout demand stabilizes and foreign equity flows normalize. State Street's Choi characterized the Taiwan dollar as "one of the best hedge currencies to US dollar strength" given its strong capital and current account flows combined with low volatility characteristics.
